## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kosiyajātaka* (Ja 470), rendered in English as "Kosiya the Miser", is an entry within the Pali *Jātaka* collection. In the standard redaction of the canonical collection and its commentary (*Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*), the entry does not provide an independent narrative of its own; rather, it consists of a concise editorial cross-reference noting that the birth story of Kosiya will be related under the *Sudhābhojanajātaka* (*Kosiyajātakaṃ Sudhābhojanajātake āvibhavissati*) [Fausböll 1887].

 This textual identity is fully corroborated by DharmaNexus, which records four shared passages amounting to 2,944 characters between Ja 470 and Ja 535 (§1.1–21.4 ↔ §1.1–21.4 with 0.99 similarity), alongside 34 matches with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Pañcamo bhāgo) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus detects automated matches between Ja 470 and the Buddhist Hybrid Sanskrit *Mahāvastu-avadāna* (53 matches, plausibility score up to 85) as well as three matches with the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (中阿含經, T 26) [DharmaNexus].
